simulator.loadTitle: How far does this go? Measured numbers and arithmetic
simulator.loadMeasuredStep5: Measured with k6 in step 5, on one 4-core sandbox shared with k6 and Redis: one gateway answered 1,000 joins and 2,000 status polls a second at p95 23 ms and 13 ms and saturated near 4,000 requests a second; one core took 500 holds a second at p95 32 ms and saturated near 900 holds a second.
simulator.loadMeasuredRun: This run: {rps} requests a second on average over the run, {peak} in its busiest second; p95 over the run so far (sampled): {join} ms to join, {status} ms per status poll, {hold} ms per hold.
simulator.loadNoRun: Start a run to see its own measured numbers here.
simulator.loadMath: 100,000 fans polling every 10 seconds make about 10,000 status polls a second. One sandbox gateway sustained 2,000 polls a second at p95 13 ms, so about 5 gateways of that size would carry the steady polling, assuming throughput grows in step with instances and one Redis keeps up. The opening burst comes on top: when most fans join in the first seconds, their joins add to the polls until the line is drawn, so the gateways need headroom above that steady figure. None of this was measured here; step 12 measures throughput on the cluster.
simulator.loadCap: Limits enforced here: at most {max} simulated fans and at most 1,500 requests a second per run; one run at a time on the whole cluster, which every environment shares; at most 3 runs an hour per organiser; and no run while a real sale on this platform has fans in its waiting room. A run still adds load to the shared cluster while it lasts.

simulator.loadSandboxTitle: Measured in a sandbox (step 5), not on this cluster

simulator.errorHourly: At most 3 runs an hour per organiser. Try again later.
